0|435b71be20f2ad3688acd94c05e968e029464d60|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"md: improve the is_mddev_idle test
During a 'resync' or similar activity
column2: md checks if the devices in the

column1: array are otherwise active and winds back resync activity when they are.
This test in done in is_mddev_idle
column2: and it is somewhat fragile - it

column1: sometimes thinks there is non-sync io when there isn't.
The test compares the total sectors of io (disk_stat_read) with the sectors
of resync io (disk->sync_io).  This has problems because total sectors gets
updated when a request completes
column2: while resync io gets updated when the

column1: request is submitted.  The time difference can cause large differenced
between the two which do not actually imply non-resync activity.  The test
currently allows for some fuzz (+/- 4096) but there are some cases when it
is not enough.
The test currently looks for any (non-fuzz) difference
negative.  This clearly is not needed.  Any non-sync activity will cause
the total sectors to grow faster than the sync_io count (never slower) so
we only need to look for a positive differences.
If we do this then the amount of in-flight sync io will never cause the
appearance of non-sync IO.  Once enough non-sync IO to worry about starts
happening
column2: resync will be slowed down and the measurements will thus be

column1: more precise (as there is less in-flight) and control of resync will still
be suitably responsive.
